{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-diag-notation}
#### $\diag$ notation

For numbers $d_1, \ldots, d_p$,
$\diag(d_1, \ldots, d_p)$ is the $p \times p$ diagonal matrix
with diagonal entries $d_1, \ldots, d_p$.
For example,

$$
\diag(2, 5) = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix},
$$

and the $p \times p$ identity matrix is $\matr{I}_p = \diag(1, \ldots, 1)$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-diagonal}
#### A matrix that is not diagonal

$\matr{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$ is not diagonal: its off-diagonal entry $d_{12} = 1 \ne 0$.

:::
